10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a simplified speech-to-text style mapping, already covered in this topic, from audio-like feature sequences to text tokens.

code.content:
import random
random.seed(0)

def simulate_audio_features(word):
    # already covered as speech-to-text starting from audio, in this topic
    random.seed(hash(word) % 1000)
    return [round(random.uniform(-1, 1), 2) for _ in range(4)]

vocabulary = ["hello", "world", "how", "are", "you"]
audio_to_text_map = {tuple(simulate_audio_features(w)): w for w in vocabulary}

def transcribe(audio_features, audio_to_text_map):
    # already covered as speech to text in this topic
    best_match, best_distance = None, float("inf")
    for features, word in audio_to_text_map.items():
        distance = sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(audio_features, features))
        if distance < best_distance:
            best_match, best_distance = word, distance
    return best_match

test_audio = simulate_audio_features("world")  # already covered as an audio waveform, simplified, in this topic
transcribed_word = transcribe(test_audio, audio_to_text_map)
print(f"Simulated audio features (already covered in this topic): {test_audio}")
print(f"Transcribed word (already covered as speech to text in this topic): '{transcribed_word}'")
